answer: Agents mapping a mesa, ridge or reef could earn admission weight from a scarce public lottery of certified survey instruments. Each instrument has one manufacturer-attested key, and a registry allows only one active agent binding per key; replacement revokes the prior binding. Random calibration checks reject emulators and cloned readings. Thousands of aliases still share one instrument quota. More weight requires purchasing additional certified instruments and maintaining calibration, imposing real capital and upkeep costs.
